## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Confirmed implementation gap remains |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | High — impossible required checks can still be described too narrowly and remediation is not consistently actionable |
| Task Type | Bug fix / verification safety |

### What Was Claimed

Issue `#94` reports that a structurally valid required local check such as root `npm test` in a monorepo without a root test script survives setup and writer execution, and that the immutable command policy cannot bind a check to the package where it is valid.

### What We Found

The current base already contains a partial fix: `VerificationCommandPolicy` has a validated repository-relative `cwd`; `resolveVerificationCommandDirectory` rejects missing directories, control directories, and symlink escapes; `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` checks required executables and statically inspects the selected package manifest; `ForgeWorkOnController.startIssue` invokes that preflight after worktree creation but before repository context loading, agent materialization, or any writer launch. `forge_verify` uses the same resolved cwd. The README documents package-scoped commands and CI-only `commands: {}`.

The remaining safety gap is in the static package-manager recognition and user-facing failure contract. `packageScriptName` only recognizes a command when its first manager argument is exactly `test`, `run`, or `run-script`; equivalent approved forms such as `npm t` are allowed through without checking the package script and can fail only after implementation. Preflight failures use an absolute caller-selected config path and a non-standard path separator (`<config> verification.commands.<name>`) and only the missing-script branch contains concrete remediation. Missing directories and executables do not consistently tell the operator to run `/forge:init` or update the exact tracked command. Existing tests cover the basic `npm test` monorepo fixture but not command aliases or the complete remediation contract.

### Root Cause

Preflight is a static safety layer, but its package-script classifier is incomplete and its error construction is distributed across branches without one actionable tracked-policy remediation. This leaves semantically impossible but structurally valid command forms able to reach the post-implementation verifier and makes setup repair less deterministic for operators.

### Affected Files

| File | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Harden package-manager script classification and centralize exact policy-path remediation. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Add alias and failure-message regression coverage using a root-without-script / `web`-with-script fixture. |
| `README.md` | Document the complete static preflight failure/remediation contract. |

### Evidence

- `src/core/policy.ts` normalizes `verification.commands.<name>.cwd` and defaults it to `.`.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts:906-910` preflights the prepared integration worktree before spawning repository writers.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts:57-60` checks package scripts only for the currently recognized invocation forms.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts:172` includes remediation only for the missing-script case.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts:63-82` proves `npm test` fails at root and succeeds at `web`, but does not cover aliases or all remediation paths.
- `src/ui/commands.ts:438-446` intentionally emits `commands: {}` for `/forge:init`, which is a valid explicit CI-only fallback rather than a package auto-detection path.

### History Findings

No history mutation or external repository access was performed. The trusted base already includes the cwd/preflight feature, so this implementation is scoped to closing the residual static-classification and remediation gaps rather than duplicating that feature.

### Recommendation

Keep the safe repository-relative cwd contract. Recognize supported npm-compatible test aliases and option forms without executing package code; fail closed for malformed/unsupported script invocations where static intent cannot be established. Route every required-command preflight failure through one formatter that includes the exact tracked config path, command name, and either a concrete config edit or `/forge:init` CI-only remediation. Extend regression tests for aliases, missing directories, missing executables, malformed package manifests, and the monorepo fixture.

### Related Issues

None identified in the trusted repository context.

### Decomposition Assessment

This is a bounded single-writer change. It does not require product, UX, protected-branch, security-authority, or schema migration decisions. No decomposition is needed.

### Acceptance Spec

- [x] Required commands can bind to a safe repository-relative package cwd.
- [x] Root `npm test` with no root script is rejected before writer launch.
- [x] A package-scoped `npm test` is accepted without executing it during preflight.
- [ ] Equivalent approved package-manager test forms are statically checked before implementation.
- [ ] Every preflight failure names the exact tracked policy location and actionable `/forge:init` or config remediation.
- [x] `commands: {}` remains an explicit GitHub-CI-only configuration.
- [x] Post-implementation required-check failures remain fail-closed through `forge_verify` and the review gate.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Contract revision | `1` |
| Allowed paths | `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts`, `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`, `README.md` |
| Forbidden changes | No changes outside the allowed paths; no policy-schema weakening; no command execution during preflight; no GitHub, branch, merge, label, or issue operations; no changes to protected-branch or lease authority; no direct `.pi/forge` artifact writes |
| Public behavior | Required checks fail before any repository writer when their executable, cwd, package manifest, or recognized package script is impossible; package-scoped commands remain supported |
| Compatibility | `cwd` remains optional and defaults to `.`; existing `npm test` and CI-only `commands: {}` behavior remains valid; non-package commands continue to use executable/cwd checks only |
| Security invariants | Resolve and canonicalize cwd beneath the repository; reject symlink escapes and Forge/Git control directories; inspect package JSON only; never spawn a repository command during preflight |
| Error contract | Preserve the exact policy location on `VerificationPreflightError.path`; include actionable tracked-config remediation and `/forge:init` CI-only fallback in every required-command failure |
| Verification | Named bound `check` must pass during verify |

### Acceptance Mapping

- [x] Preserve safe repository-relative command cwd and package selection.
- [x] Reject root package-manager test commands when the selected package has no matching script.
- [ ] Statically recognize supported test aliases such as `npm t` before implementation.
- [ ] Include exact config location and concrete remediation for missing executable, missing cwd, invalid package metadata, and missing script.
- [x] Keep optional checks skipped during preflight and keep CI-only `commands: {}` valid.
- [x] Preserve fail-closed post-implementation verification behavior.

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

`src/core/policy.ts` already validates and normalizes `verification.commands.<name>.cwd`. `src/workflows/work-on.ts` calls `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` on the prepared frozen-base worktree before loading context, materializing agents, or launching a writer. `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` resolves the same cwd before `forge_verify`. Therefore this plan does not add another launch path or alter runtime authority; it hardens the shared static adapter.

The fixture at `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` represents the reported monorepo: root `package.json` has dependencies but no scripts, while `web/package.json` defines `test`; a fake executable proves checks are static and do not run commands. Existing visible assertions require the current `VerificationPreflightError.path` shape, so the implementation will retain it while making the message uniformly actionable.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Add one remediation formatter in `verification-preflight.ts` that retains each precise policy path and explains how to set the command cwd/argv or run `/forge:init` for explicit CI-only verification.
2. Apply the formatter to required-command failures for missing directories, unavailable executables, missing/invalid package manifests, and missing scripts.
3. Extend static package-manager recognition to test aliases and option-tolerant command forms without executing npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun or changing command argv.
4. Add regression assertions covering `npm t` against the root-without-script fixture, successful package-scoped aliases, and actionable paths/remediation for missing cwd and executable failures.
5. Update README verification guidance to describe the complete fail-closed preflight and repair options.
6. Inspect the resulting diff, run the required named `check`, create the implementation commit, prepare the PR, and submit a fresh full reviewer panel.

### Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Misclassifying a non-script package-manager command | Recognize only explicit test/run forms and leave unrelated commands on executable/cwd validation |
| Accidentally executing repository code | Keep preflight limited to `access`, `stat`, `realpath`, and JSON `readFile`; add static fake-executable tests |
| Breaking existing policy consumers | Preserve default cwd, error path compatibility, and CI-only empty command map |
| Hiding a required failure behind generic remediation | Include command name and exact `.forge/config.json` policy path in every thrown error |

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
